chapter: The levee club and the St. Louis scene
title: Describing a player's style: Sleepy Tomlin and Shorty Baker
summary: Dance asks how to describe unrecorded trumpeters. Thomas refuses to compare players but calls Hal (Shorty) Baker the greatest trumpet player he ever heard.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: No, you can't actually compare but the only thing is you, when you're trying to say, now how did the guy play. Well, for the sake if you could say, well, just of argument somebody like that Sleepy Tomlin, now if you wanted to say who did he play like. Well, we have no records so if you could say, well, he used to sound a little bit like Joe Smith or he used to sound a little bit like Louis Armstrong. Well then you have a little idea of where he was at. That's all you can do.
Because you can't accurately describe a musical style, can you? I mean if you can take a record, that's another thing.

Never. Somebody has got to get somebody. I figure that way. Now, to give you an idea of what I mean since you gave me that idea, it could have been near to Joe Smith. Because Joe Smith was a great trumpet player I think.

Yeah, well, that's what I thought. Just as you say you went to those three trumpet player's studio, well, all these people you can hear on records even if you couldn't hear them in person and it would give you an idea.
Well, sometimes you couldn't afford to get to hear them in person.

You know, that's the damnedest idea and maybe sometimes you were too young to hear them in person but I mean to make a comparison, a miserable comparison, I'm going to try to do it. But, I mean to hear I think Sleepy was -- no, I think it's wonderful, I'm glad you brought him up.

Well, listen, he's a good buddy. He was like Hal Baker, you know. Hal Baker was a tremendous trumpet player and we talked about a lot of things. And he flowed but to compare him with anybody, I think he would really, I think Hal Baker to me was probably the greatest trumpet player I've ever heard in my life.

If you were trying to describe ... to somebody you've never heard of, well, basically, there was a little more in common between what Shorty did and Joe Smith, than Shorty and Louis, wouldn't you say?
